paper.title: Internal Regret with Partial Monitoring. Calibration-Based Optimal Algorithms

unmapped: Regret is internal regret (swap of action i by k on stages where i was played), stronger than external regret
Learner knows the payoff matrix rho (finite game with J Nature actions)
Nature's strategy may depend on history
settings.definition_quote: Consider a two-person game $\Gamma$ repeated in discrete time, where at stage $n$, a decision maker ... chooses an action $i_n \in \mathcal{I}$ (resp. $j_n \in \mathcal{J}$). This generates a payoff $\rho_n=\rho(i_n,j_n)$ ...

settings.name_in_paper: Partial monitoring with outcome dependent signals (internal regret)
unmapped: Signal laws do not depend on the decision maker's action (s(i,.) = s(i',.))
Random signals; regret measured with the worst-case payoff W(x,f) compatible with the flag (Rustichini / Lehrer-Solan internal regret over mixed-action types)
Learner knows payoff and signal functions
settings.definition_quote: In this section, we assume that the laws of the signal received by the decision maker are independent of his action. Formally, for every $i, i' \in \mathcal{I}$, the two mappings $s(i,\cdot)$ and $s(i',\cdot)$ are equal.

settings.name_in_paper: Partial monitoring with action-outcome dependent signals (internal regret)
unmapped: Random signals whose law depends on action and outcome; regret measured with worst-case compatible payoff W(x,f) (internal regret over mixed-action types)
Learner knows payoff and signal functions
settings.definition_quote: In this section, we consider the most general framework and we assume that the laws of the signals might depend on the decision maker's actions.

settings.name_in_paper: Compact case: Nature chooses outcome vectors in [-1,1]^I and flags (polytopial graph)
unmapped: Nature's outcome set is compact (not finite); flag chosen in multivalued s(O_n) with polytopial graph
Internal regret with worst-case compatible payoff
settings.definition_quote: Assume that instead of choosing $j_n$ ... Nature chooses directly an outcome vector $O_n \in [-1,1]^I$ and a flag $f_n$ which belongs to $\mathbf{s}(O_n)$ where $\mathbf{s}$ is a multivalued mapping from $[-1,1]^I$ into $\Delta(\mathcal{S})^I$.

algorithms.name: Calibration w.r.t. Laguerre diagram refining best-response areas (tool algorithm, full monitoring)
Laguerre-calibration-based strategy with gamma_n-perturbation and importance-weighted flag estimates

source.label: regreinternnul
source.quote: There exists an internally consistent strategy $\sigma$ of the forecaster such that for every strategy~$\tau$ of Nature and every $n \in \mathbb{N}$, with $\mathbb{P}_{\sigma,\tau}$ probability greater than $1-\delta$: \max_{i,k \in \mathcal{I}} \bar{R}_{n}^{ik}\leq O\left(\sqrt{\frac{\ln\left(\frac{1}{\delta}\right)}{n}}\right).

results.notes: Bound on average internal regret multiplied by T. Paper notes this result is already well known; constants depend on L (exponential in J). Internal regret (implies external). Comparator set to best_fixed_action as closest proxy.

conditions: signal laws independent of the decision maker's action

source.label: theooutcome
source.quote: There exists an internally consistent strategy $\sigma$ such that for every strategy~$\tau$ of Nature, with $\mathbb{P}_{\sigma,\tau}$-probability at least $1- \delta$: \sup_{l \in \mathcal{L}}\frac{|N_n(l)|}{n}\mathcal{R}_{n}(l) \leq O\left(\sqrt{\frac{\ln\left(\frac{1}{\delta}\right)}{n}}\right).

results.notes: Average internal regret (worst-case compatible payoff) multiplied by T. Computational cost polynomial in L (constant size per stage). Constants depend on L, M_P, M_W, S.

source.label: theoaction
source.quote: There exists an internally consistent strategy $\sigma$ such that, for every strategy~$\tau$ of Nature, with $\mathbb{P}_{\sigma,\tau}$ probability at least $1- \delta$: \max_{l \in \mathcal{L}}\frac{|N_n(l)|}{n}\mathcal{R}_{n}(l)\leq O\left(\frac{1}{n^{1/3}}\sqrt{\ln\left(\frac{1}{\delta}\right)}+\frac{1}{n^{2/3}}\ln\left(\frac{1}{\delta}\right)\right).

results.notes: Average internal regret multiplied by T. Main result; also bounds external regret. Paper claims optimal via label-efficient lower bound. Complexity polynomial in L (paper calls it efficient 'in some sense'). Proof gives explicit constants Omega_1..Omega_5 depending on L, I, S, M_P, M_W, M_rho.

conditions: the graph of the signal correspondence s is a polytope

source.label: theocompact
source.quote: If the graph of  $\mathbf{s}$  is a polytope, then there exists an internally consistent strategy $\sigma$ such that, for every strategy $\tau$ of Nature, with $\mathds{P}_{\sigma,\tau}$ probability at least $1- \delta$: \max_{l \in \mathcal{L}}\frac{|N_n(l)|}{n}\mathcal{R}_{n}(l)\leq O\left(\frac{1}{n^{1/3}}\sqrt{\ln\left(\frac{1}{\delta}\right)}+\frac{1}{n^{2/3}}\ln\left(\frac{1}{\delta}\right)\right).

results.notes: Average internal regret multiplied by T. Proof identical to Theorem theoaction.
